questions.question: When doing an offset back/left parking maneuver, what should you do?

options.text: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
Pull forward to the right, then back in a straight line.
Pull forward to the left, then back in a straight line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/left parking maneuver, pull straight forward first. Then back up to the left. Your vehicle must stay completely within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: When evacuating a school bus, students should be led at least ____ away from the road.
questions.correctAnswerText: 100 feet
questions.explanation: During a school bus evacuation, lead students at least 100 feet from the road. The driver should lead them toward oncoming traffic. This distance protects them from flying debris if another vehicle hits the bus.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing in a school bus, what should you do?

options.text: Stop between 15 and 50 feet before the nearest rail.
Stop 100 feet before the nearest rail.
Stop 10 feet before the nearest rail.
Continue across the tracks without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop between 15 and 50 feet before the nearest rail.
questions.explanation: Stop 15 to 50 feet before the nearest rail. This distance gives you the best view of the tracks. Look and listen for trains before crossing.

questions.question: When exiting the bus during the vehicle control skills test, you must:

options.text: Keep both hands on the handrail.
Maintain a firm grasp on the handrail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain a firm grasp on the handrail.
questions.explanation: When exiting the bus, face the vehicle and maintain three points of contact at all times. Hold the handrail firmly. Exiting incorrectly can result in automatic failure of the test.

questions.question: How is student safety best maintained during an emergency?

options.text: Keeping the students on the bus.
Letting some students evacuate while others stay on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeping the students on the bus.
questions.explanation: In most emergencies, students are safest when they stay on the bus. They remain under control and protected.

questions.question: A properly adjusted flat mirror should show the driver:

options.text: The rear tires touching the ground.
The front tires touching the ground.
Only the roadway and no parts of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rear tires touching the ground.
questions.explanation: A properly adjusted flat mirror shows 200 feet behind the bus, the base of each rear wheel, and the sides of the bus.

questions.question: During the steering box inspection, which action should you NOT do?

options.text: Ensure that the steering box is securely mounted.
Ensure that the steering box is free of leaks.
Look for missing bolts in the steering box.
Assume all cotter keys are present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume all cotter keys are present.
questions.explanation: Check that the steering box is securely mounted. Look for missing nuts, bolts, and cotter keys. Check for power steering fluid leaks and damaged hoses. Do not assume cotter keys are present.

questions.question: A school bus stop:

options.text: Can be added by the driver if students are given notice.
Should be voted on by students and parents.
Should be established by the school and not changed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be established by the school and not changed.
questions.explanation: Never change or add a bus stop without written approval from school district officials.

questions.question: During the on-road test, you will be checked on traffic awareness. Which should you NOT do?

options.text: Avoid checking your mirrors near intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid checking your mirrors near intersections.
questions.explanation: Check mirrors and traffic regularly, especially at intersections. Scan for pedestrians wherever they might be present.

questions.question: When exiting your vehicle, you must maintain ____ with the vehicle at all times.
questions.correctAnswerText: Three points of contact
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle, face it and keep three points of contact at all times. For a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly can result in automatic failure of the test.

questions.question: On a bus with outside convex mirrors, where are they located?
questions.correctAnswerText: Below the outside flat mirrors.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors on a school bus are located below the flat mirrors. They help the driver see a wide area around the bus, including traffic, clearance, and students.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, the landing gear must be:

options.text: More worn on the passenger's side than on the driver's side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fully raised.
questions.explanation: Check that the landing gear has no missing parts and is fully raised. The crank handle must be secure, and the support frame must not be damaged.

questions.question: If a school bus must be evacuated, passengers should:

options.text: Use the exit that is safest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the exit that is safest.
questions.explanation: During an emergency evacuation, the driver must quickly decide which exit is safest and direct students to use it.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing while driving a placarded vehicle, you should always:

options.text: Stop within five feet of the tracks.
Change gears while on the tracks.
Change lanes while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: Before crossing railroad tracks, stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail. Turn on your four-way flashers while crossing. Do not change gears or lanes while any part of your vehicle is on the tracks.

questions.question: If the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops working:

options.text: You should only use the parking brake to stop.
You should stop driving and wait for ABS to work again.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will still have brakes.
questions.explanation: ABS is added to a vehicle's braking system to prevent brake lock-up during hard braking. If ABS fails, your regular brakes will still work. You can continue driving and braking normally.

questions.question: Loading and unloading a school bus:

options.text: Can be done while talking to another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be dangerous for passengers.
questions.explanation: More students are hurt or killed during loading and unloading than while riding the bus. Drivers must follow safety procedures and properly supervise this process.

questions.question: During the expressway driving test, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors to monitor traffic.
Drive on the left side of your lane.
Drive faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors to monitor traffic.
questions.explanation: On the expressway during the driving test, keep your position in the lane, maintain safe distance from other vehicles, and follow the speed limit. Always check your mirrors and look for traffic in all directions.

questions.question: Passive railroad crossings:

options.text: Usually have a flagger directing traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not have control devices.
questions.explanation: Passive railroad crossings have no traffic control devices. The driver is responsible for deciding when it is safe to cross the tracks.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you should:

options.text: Choose your own route to show your skills.
Listen to and follow the examiner's directions.
Bring a passenger to ride with you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen to and follow the examiner's directions.
questions.explanation: Follow all directions given by the examiner during the test. The examiner will never ask you to drive unsafely.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to:

options.text: Pull forward into a parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alley dock.
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset backing, parallel parking on both sides, and alley docking.
